strings.App.Title: Steam Pipe Manager
strings.Profile.Title: Choose a profile
strings.Profile.Subtitle: Each store account is a profile. Games and side apps like demos and playtests live under it.
strings.Profile.Empty.Title: No profiles yet
strings.Profile.Empty.Body: Create a profile for each store account. If you already publish through SteamPipe, you can import your existing ContentBuilder folders in one click — no manual data entry.
strings.Profile.Name: Profile name
strings.Profile.Username.Hint: The name SteamCMD signs in with — your Steamworks account username.
strings.Profile.Edit.Title: Edit profile
strings.Profile.Edit.Warning: Changing the username clears the session and avatar; you will need to sign in again with the new account.
strings.Profile.New.Title: New profile
strings.Profile.NoPassword.Title: No password needed here
strings.Profile.NoPassword.Body: After creating the profile, sign in once from its card. The app never sees or stores your password.
strings.Profile.Error.Required: Profile name and Steam username are required.
strings.Profile.Error.UsernameTaken: '{0}' is already used by another profile.
strings.Profile.Delete.Title: Delete profile
strings.Profile.Delete.HasApps: Its {0} games and {1} build target definitions will be deleted too.
strings.Profile.Delete.NoApps: This profile has no games defined.
strings.Login.Title: Sign in to Steam
strings.Login.Note: Your password is kept in memory only while signing in; it is never written to disk or passed on the command line. After that SteamCMD remembers the session itself.
strings.Login.Mobile.Title: Confirm on your phone
strings.Login.Mobile.Body: A sign-in request was sent to the Steam Mobile app. This window closes once you approve it.
strings.Login.Error.RateLimit: Too many attempts. Steam is refusing new sign-ins for a while; wait a few minutes.
strings.Login.Error.GuardRequired: A Steam Guard code is required.
strings.Apps.Title: Choose a game
strings.Apps.Empty.Title: No games in this profile yet
strings.Apps.Empty.Body: Add a game from scratch, or — on Steam profiles — import the ContentBuilder folders you already use, so you don't have to retype anything.
strings.Import.Title: Import a ContentBuilder setup
strings.Import.Body: Point at the SDK root, the tools\ContentBuilder folder, or the scripts folder directly. Your existing app_*.vdf files will be read and turned into build targets.
strings.Workspace.AddSubApp.Tip: Add another build target such as a demo, playtest or beta
strings.Workspace.SelectPrompt: Pick a build target on the left, or add a new one.
strings.General.Title: Title
strings.General.SharedContent.Hint: leave empty — each depot uses its own folder
strings.Depot.Label: Label
strings.Build.LogHidden: The detailed SteamCMD output is hidden. It opens automatically if something goes wrong, and you can open it any time with the log button.
strings.Build.Branch.Note: If empty, the build is uploaded but no branch is set live.
strings.Build.PreviewToggle: Preview build — nothing is uploaded, it only reports what would be
strings.Build.Summary.NoBranch: none — will not be set live
strings.Build.GoesLive: When this build finishes it will be set live on {0} and players on that branch get the update immediately.
strings.Build.Confirm.Title: Build will go live
strings.Build.Confirm.Body:
When this build finishes it will be set live on '{0}' and players on that branch will get the update immediately.

Game: {1}
Target: {2} (AppID {3})

Continue?
strings.Build.TargetInvalid: This target has problems to fix. See the Build tab.
strings.Preview.Note: The exact contents of the files that will be written when you build. These files are regenerated before every build; manual edits are not kept.
strings.History.Empty: No builds for this target yet.
strings.History.OpenLog.Tip: Show this build's log file in Explorer
strings.History.NoLog: The log file for this build was not found.
strings.Settings.Title: Settings
strings.Settings.Language.Body: Language files live in the folder below. Drop your own JSON file there to add a language — no rebuild needed.
strings.Settings.SteamCmd.Body: All profiles share one SteamCMD installation — no need to copy the SDK per game. Leave empty and the app downloads Valve's public build itself.
strings.Settings.SteamCmd.Placeholder: empty = let the app download it
strings.Settings.SteamCmd.Verify.Tip: Check whether a working steamcmd is at this path
strings.Settings.Timeouts.Body: If a session or credential has expired, the publishing tool can sit waiting on a prompt we cannot see. These limits stop it from hanging.
strings.Settings.StallSeconds.Hint: If the publishing tool's log stops growing for this long during a build, the run is stopped.
strings.Settings.DataLocation.Body: Profiles, generated scripts, build output and history are kept here. profiles.json contains no passwords; it is safe to back up and share.
strings.Settings.OpenFolder.Tip: Open the data folder in Explorer
strings.Settings.SteamCmd.NotFound: No steamcmd.exe found at this path.
strings.Settings.SteamCmd.Empty: Path is empty — the app will download its own copy when building.
strings.Setup.Intro: Manage every store account, game and side app from one place. One tool installation is shared by all of them — no more copying an SDK per game.
strings.Setup.SteamCmd.Body: SteamCMD uploads your builds to Steam. The app can download Valve's public build for you, or use one you already have. You can also do this later — it will be downloaded before your first build.
strings.Validate.TooManyMain: '{0}' has {1} targets marked as the main game; only one is allowed.
strings.Validate.TargetNameRequired: The build target's name cannot be empty.
strings.Validate.ForbiddenBranch: '{0}': a build cannot be set live on '{1}' directly. Switching the default branch is done on the Steamworks site.
strings.Validate.DepotIdRequired: '{0}' has a depot with no DepotID.
strings.Validate.MappingRequired: {0}: at least one file mapping is required.
strings.Validate.NoContentRoot: {0}: no content folder is set, on the depot or the build target.
strings.Validate.ContentEmpty: {0}: content folder is empty — {1}. Uploading an empty depot would delete the content currently live on Steam, so the build is blocked.
strings.Build.AlreadyRunning: A build is already running. Only one build runs at a time.
strings.Build.NeedsLogin: SteamCMD asked for credentials; the session has expired. Sign in again and retry.
strings.Session.PasswordAsked: SteamCMD asked for a password; the cached session is no longer valid.
strings.Session.NotVerified: Sign-in could not be verified (exit code {0}).
strings.Login.Timeout: Sign-in timed out. It may have been waiting for Steam Guard approval.
strings.Import.NoAppScripts: No app build scripts found under '{0}'.
strings.Import.BadDepotId: '{0}' is not a valid DepotID, skipped.
strings.Import.NoDepots: No depots found; you will need to add them after importing.
strings.Import.SdkSample: A sample file that ships with the Steamworks SDK; not a real game.
strings.Import.DepotScriptUnreadable: Script for depot {0} could not be read ({1}): {2}
strings.Build.NotFinished: The build did not finish (exit code {0}).
strings.Apps.Edit.Title: Rename game
strings.Apps.Delete.Title: Delete game
strings.Apps.Delete.Body:
Delete the game '{0}'?

Its {1} build target definitions will be deleted too.

Generated scripts, build output and your game files are untouched — only this app's definitions are removed.
strings.Workspace.Delete.Title: Delete build target
strings.Workspace.Delete.Body:
Delete the build target '{0}' (AppID {1})?

Generated scripts and build history stay on disk — only the definition is removed.
strings.Depot.Delete.Title: Delete depot
strings.Depot.Delete.Body:
Delete depot {0}?

Only the definition is removed — the content folder is untouched. A build target missing a depot uploads incomplete content, so add it back before building.
strings.Epic.CredentialsRejected: Epic rejected these credentials. Check the Client ID and Client Secret on the product's BPT Credentials page.
strings.Epic.CheckNotVerified: The credentials could not be verified (exit code {0}).
strings.Epic.Version.Required: A build version is required. BuildPatchTool accepts an empty one, but the build would have no name on Epic.
strings.Epic.Version.ForbiddenCharacters: The build version cannot contain these characters: {0}
strings.Epic.Version.TooLong: The build version is longer than {0} characters.
strings.Epic.Version.SpacesRemoved: BuildPatchTool strips spaces, so this will be recorded as '{0}'.
strings.Epic.Validate.ArtifactIdRequired: The Artifact ID is required. You can find it in the Dev Portal under the product's artifacts.
strings.Epic.Validate.ProfileIncomplete: This profile is missing its Organization ID or Client ID.
strings.Epic.Validate.ProductIdRequired: The Product ID is required for this game.
strings.Epic.Validate.BuildRootEmpty: The content folder has no data in it — {0}. BuildPatchTool refuses a folder that holds only empty files.
strings.Epic.Validate.AppLaunchRequired: The path to the game executable is required.
strings.Epic.Validate.AppLaunchMissing: The executable was not found inside the content folder — {0}
strings.Epic.Validate.PlatformRequired: A platform name is required when a label is set; BuildPatchTool needs both together.
strings.Epic.UploadedButNotLabelled: The build was uploaded as '{0}' but could not be set live on '{1}'. It exists on Epic; you only need to retry the labelling. Reason: {2}
strings.Epic.Experimental: Epic support is experimental: it has not yet been verified against a real Epic publisher account. Everything is measured against the real BuildPatchTool, but a live upload has not been tested.
strings.Epic.Credentials.Hint: From the Dev Portal: your product's Product Settings → BPT Credentials. These are separate from your game's EOS SDK credentials.
strings.Epic.SecretStorage.Title: Where the secret is kept
strings.Epic.SecretStorage.Body: Unlike Steam, Epic needs the secret to persist. It is encrypted with Windows DPAPI into a separate file, so profiles.json stays free of credentials and safe to back up or share.
strings.Epic.Error.Required: Profile name, Organization ID and Client ID are required.
strings.Epic.SecretUnchanged: A secret is already stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
strings.Epic.ToolPathMissing: BuildPatchTool has not been set up. Point Settings at your own copy — Epic does not allow us to download it for you.
strings.Epic.SecretMissing: No client secret is stored for this profile. Add it from the profile's edit screen.
strings.Epic.Tool.Body: Epic uploads go through BuildPatchTool. Unlike SteamCMD we cannot download it for you — it sits behind the Epic Dev Portal. Download it there (Epic Games Store → Artifacts and Binaries), unzip it, and point at the folder or the exe.
strings.Epic.Tool.Pick.Tip: Pick BuildPatchTool.exe or the folder it was unzipped into
strings.Epic.Tool.Verify.Tip: Check whether BuildPatchTool is at this path
strings.Epic.Tool.Empty: No path is set. Epic profiles cannot publish until BuildPatchTool is set up.
strings.Epic.Tool.NotFound: BuildPatchTool was not found at this path. Pick the unzipped folder or the exe inside Engine\Binaries\Win64.
strings.Epic.NoTargetToCheck: Add a game with a Product ID and an artifact first. Epic credentials can only be checked against a real target — BuildPatchTool validates the arguments before it ever reaches authentication.
strings.Epic.AddArtifact.Tip: Add another artifact, for example a second platform or a demo
strings.Epic.SelectPrompt: Pick an artifact on the left, or add a new one.
strings.Epic.Delete.Title: Delete artifact
strings.Epic.Delete.Body:
Delete the artifact '{0}' ({1})?

Only this app's definition is removed. Anything already uploaded to Epic stays there.
strings.Epic.ProductId.Hint: Belongs to the game, not to a single artifact — all artifacts of this game share it.
strings.Epic.BuildRoot.Hint: Epic has no depots: one artifact means one content folder. Use separate artifacts for separate platforms.
strings.Epic.CloudDir.Hint: Keeping it lets BuildPatchTool recognise data it already uploaded, so later updates download smaller for players.
strings.Epic.BuildVersionTemplate.Hint: Unlike Steam, Epic does not hand you a build number — you supply it, and reusing one collides. The app generates the next unused version from this template.
strings.Epic.Label: Label to set live
strings.Epic.Label.Hint: Applying a label is a second call after the upload. If the upload succeeds but the label fails, the build sits on Epic without going live — the app tells you so you can retry just the labelling.
strings.Epic.PreviewToggle: Dry run — validates arguments, credentials and backend state without uploading anything
strings.Epic.Step.Label: 2. Set live
strings.Epic.Preview.Note: The exact commands that will run. Epic generates no script files — everything is passed as arguments.
strings.Epic.Preview.SecretNote: # The client secret is not on the command line: it is passed to the tool through an environment variable, so it never appears in the process list.
strings.Epic.Preview.VersionNote: # BuildPatchTool strips spaces from the version, so Epic will record this build as '{0}'.
strings.Epic.Build.Tip: Upload the build to Epic, then apply the label if one is set
strings.Epic.Preview.Tip: Dry run — validates everything without uploading
strings.Epic.PartialFailure: The build was uploaded but could not be set live. It exists on Epic — you only need to retry, and the upload will be recognised.
strings.Epic.PreviewDone: Dry run finished — nothing was uploaded.
strings.Epic.Confirm.Body:
When this build finishes it will be labelled '{0}' and players on that label get the update immediately.

Game: {1}
Artifact: {2} ({3})

Continue?
strings.Epic.ExportLog.Tip: Save a shareable copy of the log. Organization, product and artifact IDs, your user name and home paths are masked; the technical lines are kept.
strings.Apps.QuickBuild.Tip: Build and send now — opens the Build tab and starts straight away
strings.Settings.Updates.Body: New versions come from the project's GitHub releases. A download is installed only if it matches the SHA-256 checksum published with the release; if anything goes wrong, the current version is kept.
strings.Settings.Updates.AutoCheck: Check for updates when the app starts
strings.Settings.Updates.CheckNow.Tip: Ask GitHub for the latest release
strings.Update.Banner.ManualOnly: Version {0} is available, but it cannot be installed from inside the app: {1}
strings.Update.Install.Tip: Download the new version, verify it, replace the app files and restart
strings.Update.BlockedByBuild: A build is running. Update once it has finished.
strings.Update.Reason.DevelopmentBuild: this copy was not started from a release package.
strings.Update.Reason.NotWritable: the app folder is not writable. Download the new version and extract it yourself.
strings.Update.Reason.NoPackage: the release has no verified package for this app.
strings.Update.Error.Network: GitHub could not be reached. Check your connection and try again.
strings.Update.Error.RateLimited: GitHub is limiting requests right now. Try again later.
strings.Update.Error.InvalidResponse: GitHub returned a response the app does not understand.
strings.Update.Error.ChecksumMissing: the release lists no checksum for this package, so it was not installed.
strings.Update.Error.ChecksumMismatch: the download did not match its published checksum, so it was not installed.
strings.Update.Error.PackageInvalid: the package does not contain this app, so it was not installed.
strings.Update.Error.InstallFailed: the app files could not be replaced. The current version was kept.
strings.Update.Error.RestartFailed: the new version could not be started. The previous version was restored.
strings.Close.Unsaved.Title: Unsaved changes
